**VERDICT: REJECT** **Overall Assessment**: The component implements the visual and DOM structure for infinite scroll but lacks the essential assistive technology communication, keyboard operability, and landmark context required for a functional dynamic list. While `
    `/`
  • ` semantics are correctly used, the absence of `aria-live` status announcements, keyboard fallback triggers, and loading/error state management creates complete access barriers for screen reader and keyboard users. The design is 60% implemented: the visual scroll mechanic works, but the interaction model is invisible to assistive technology. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: Before reading code, I predicted: 1. Missing `aria-live` region or status announcement for dynamic list updates 2. No keyboard fallback/trigger for loading more items (violates 2.1.1) 3. Missing landmark structure and accessible name for the list 4. Undefined focus management strategy when new items append 5. Silent failure on API error (no AT communication) **Actual Findings vs Predictions**: All predictions materialized as design gaps. The component relies entirely on mouse/scroll interaction, provides zero programmatic state updates to assistive technology, and lacks structural context. No unexpected findings emerged; the gaps are foundational rather than incremental. --- ### Critical Findings (blocks access) 1. **No keyboard trigger for core infinite scroll functionality** - **Evidence**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:38-40` (`
    `) contains no interactive element, button, or keyboard shortcut to invoke `loadMore()`. - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard-only users, motor accessibility users - **Expected Behavior**: Per WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), all functionality must be operable via keyboard. Infinite scroll components require a visible "Load More" button or documented keyboard shortcut (e.g., `Enter` on the trigger region) alongside scroll behavior. - **Fix**: Replace the empty `
    ` with ``. Keep the IntersectionObserver as a progressive enhancement, but ensure the button is always present and keyboard-focusable. 2. **Dynamic list updates not communicated to assistive technology** - **Evidence**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:15-17` (`setItems((prev) => [...prev, ...newItems])`) mutates state without any `aria-live`, `role="status"`, or live region update. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) - **Expected Behavior**: Per WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages), dynamically updated content must be announced to assistive technology. Appending list items without announcement leaves screen reader users unaware that new content has loaded or that the page is still active. - **Fix**: Add a visually hidden `
    {isLoading ? 'Loading more items...' : `${newItems.length} items loaded`}
    ` and sync its text state with `loadMore()`. --- ### Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) 1. **Missing landmark structure and list accessible name** - **Evidence**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:34-35` (`
    `, `
      `) - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users, keyboard navigation users - **Expected Behavior**: Per WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and APG Landmark patterns, the list needs an accessible name (`aria-label` or heading) and should be wrapped in a landmark (`
      ` or `role="main"`) for page context. Screen readers will announce "list, 0 items" with no semantic context. - **Fix**: Wrap container in `
      `. Add `aria-label="Feed items"` to the `
        `, or wrap it in an `

        ` and use `aria-labelledby`. 2. **Loading state not communicated programmatically** - **Evidence**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:10-14` (`loadMore` function) has no loading state management or `aria-busy` toggling. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users, cognitive accessibility users - **Expected Behavior**: Per WCAG 4.1.3 and APG Feed/List patterns, a loading indicator must communicate its state via `aria-busy="true"` on the list container or an associated status region. Visual spinners alone are insufficient. - **Fix**: Add `const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);` to `loadMore()`, toggle it around the async call, and apply `aria-busy={isLoading}` to the `
          `. 3. **Undefined focus management strategy on content append** - **Evidence**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:15-17` appends items without focus relocation logic. - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard users, screen reader users - **Expected Behavior**: Per WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and APG dynamic list patterns, focus must be explicitly managed when content changes. Either keep focus in place (acceptable for infinite scroll) OR move focus to the first new item with `scrollIntoView()` + `focus()`. The design must be intentional, not accidental. - **Fix**: Document the chosen strategy. If keeping focus is intended, add a comment and ensure `aria-live` announces the update so users know content changed without focus moving. If moving focus is preferred, implement `setTimeout(() => observerTarget.current?.scrollIntoView(), 300)` after state update. --- ### Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) - **Empty trigger element lacks `aria-hidden`**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:39` (`
          `) is empty now but will likely contain a loading spinner. If it does, add `aria-hidden="true"` to prevent AT from announcing decorative content. - **No error handling for failed fetches**: `loadMore()` lacks try/catch or error state. API failures would be silent. Add `aria-live="assertive"` region for error announcements per WCAG 4.1.3. ### Enhancements (best practice not met) - Consider adding `aria-relevant="additions text"` to the live region if only new items should trigger announcements, preventing full list re-reads. - Add `prefers-reduced-motion` media query handling for scroll-triggered animations if visual transitions are added later. --- ### What's Missing (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions) - **Keyboard fallback mechanism**: No button, link, or shortcut exists to trigger `loadMore()` without scrolling. - **Live region architecture**: No `aria-live` container exists in the DOM template. - **Landmark & naming context**: List lacks accessible name; container lacks landmark role. - **Loading/error state management**: No `isLoading` state, no `aria-busy`, no error announcement path. - **Focus strategy documentation**: Append behavior is unmanaged; screen readers won't know if the page froze or updated. --- ### Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | HIGH | No live region, no landmark, list has no accessible name, loading state invisible to AT | | Keyboard-only | HIGH | Core functionality (loading more) requires scroll/mouse; no keyboard trigger or shortcut | | Low vision | MEDIUM | Focus management undefined on append; potential horizontal scroll if items wrap at 200% zoom | | Cognitive | MEDIUM | No loading feedback; silent API failures; unclear if component is working or broken | | Vestibular & motion | LOW | No animations present yet, but scroll-triggered updates can cause jarring reflows without `prefers-reduced-motion` handling | | Auditory access | LOW | No media elements present | | Environmental contrast | LOW | No color-dependent states visible in current code | --- ### Verdict Justification The component fails to meet baseline accessibility design requirements for dynamic content. The absence of a keyboard trigger (WCAG 2.1.1) and programmatic state communication (WCAG 4.1.3) are not incremental polish issues; they are foundational access barriers. Screen reader users will hear a static list with no indication of updates, and keyboard users cannot interact with the core feature without scrolling. The design must be revised to include live region announcements, keyboard fallback triggers, landmark context, and explicit focus/loading state management before implementation can proceed. **What would need to change for an upgrade**: 1.
